newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Multiple Zone CEO aims high.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Multiple Zone CEO aims high.

text.p: John DeFeo, newly appointed chief executive officer of Multiple Zones International Inc, said the company ultimately could achieve $2 billion in annual revenues, compared with about $450 million last year.
But in an interview, DeFeo declined to say when the computer hardware and software reseller might achieve that milestone.

"I think the board was looking ahead at what does it take to build a billion-dollar revenue stream company and then how do you build a $2 billion revenue stream company," DeFeo said of his appointment.
"I've done that in the past ... and I think the board just wanted the experience of someone who's been on that journey."
DeFeo previously was president and chief executive officer of U.S. West Inc's domestic cellular unit, and he founded U.S. Airwaves Inc, a wireless communications company.
Tim Carroll, a vice president, projected sales "in the $130 million range" for the fourth quarter, giving the company revenues of about $450 million for the year, compared with $243 million in 1995.
Both Carroll and DeFeo declined to comment on 1997 sales projections or on earnings estimates. The company said last month that its fourth-quarter earnings would fall short of analyst expectations.
Carroll said the shortfall was due to industrywide factors.
"It all has to due with a very weak selling season for PCs in the retail market," he said.

But he said the company's fourth-quarter sales still would be a record, and future prospects are bright as the company broadens its mission beyond its original core business of selling Macintosh-related hardware, software and peripherals to consumers through catalogs.

Carroll said the company's fastest-growing business was its direct sales to business, government and education markets. And sales of "Wintel"-based hardware and software are growing at nearly twice the rate of Macintosh-related gear.
With 4.5 million catalogs sent out each month, the catalog business will remain a significant part of the Renton, Wash.-based company's business for the foreseeable future, the executives said.
